fixes.explanation: That's it. "The LORD is righteous; He has cut me from the cords of the wicked." (Psalm 129:4) Cords are what tie something down, and the psalm says He cut Israel loose from them. The verse names the LORD as the One who did the cutting. I've been tied up in a few tight spots myself, so I know a good snip when I hear one.

Withers is the word. "May they be like grass on the rooftops, which withers before it can grow…" (Psalm 129:6) The grass never gets the chance to grow. That's the picture the psalm wishes on those who hate Zion.

Drowning is a good guess for a plant, but it's not the word in the verse. The psalm says the grass "…withers before it can grow…" (Psalm 129:6) The verse says withers and says nothing about water. I wouldn't water a rooftop, and I don't think the psalm expects you to.

Freezing would make sense if the verse were about winter, but it doesn't mention cold. The psalm says the grass on the rooftops "…withers before it can grow…" (Psalm 129:6) Withering is the word the verse uses, not a deep freeze.

That's the one. The psalm says, "May none who pass by say to them, “The blessing of the LORD be on you; we bless you in the name of the LORD.”" (Psalm 129:8) So the wish is that no one passing by would speak that blessing over them. That's how the song ends.
